title: From pendent and ancillary jurisdiction to § 1367
shortTitle: From pendent and ancillary jurisdiction to § 1367
summary: Pendent and ancillary jurisdiction are historical descriptions of federal authority over related claims or parties. Congress’s enactment of § 1367 provides the statutory framework emphasized in the later course materials.
notes: An older case’s terminology does not automatically answer the statutory question. Preserve the chronology and identify the proposition for which an older decision remains useful.

sections.Meaning: Pendent and ancillary jurisdiction are historical descriptions of federal authority over related claims or parties. Congress’s enactment of § 1367 provides the statutory framework emphasized in the later course materials.
sections.How to work through the question: Use Gibbs for the related-case and discretionary framework, then compare Aldinger, Kroger, and Finley for the difficulties of adding parties. Read the statute and Exxon to determine how its text changes the analysis.
